questions.q: Which of these belongs on the capstone's definition-of-done checklist?
options: Both services containerized, infrastructure provisioned as code, CI/CD automated with promotion gates, monitored, security-scanned, and documented
Only that the code compiles without errors
A 100% unit test coverage requirement for both services
Migrating the application to a second cloud provider
questions.explain: The definition of done is the full checklist: containerized, IaC-provisioned, CI/CD automated end to end with promotion and approval gates, monitored with alerting, security-scanned, and documented.

questions.q: Why does the project plan insist Phase 2 (Infrastructure) must be complete before Phase 3 (Pipeline & Deployment)?
options: It doesn't matter — phases can be done in any order
Because you can't automate a deploy to infrastructure that doesn't exist yet
Because GitHub Actions requires infrastructure to be provisioned manually first
Because Terraform cannot run after a CI pipeline exists
questions.explain: Each phase builds strictly on the one before it. A deployment pipeline in Phase 3 needs the AKS clusters, ACR, and networking that Phase 2's Terraform provisions — there's nothing to deploy to otherwise.

questions.q: Which lesson uses the Terraform state-locking collision as its motivating example?
options: Lesson 3, Success Criteria & Project Plan
Lesson 7, Provisioning Cloud Infrastructure With Terraform
Lesson 15, Adding Security Scanning & Secrets Management
Lesson 16, Incident Drill & Postmortem
questions.explain: The scenario where two engineers' terraform apply commands collide, with the second failing due to Azure blob-lease state locking, is the worked example for Lesson 7 and the reason remote state + locking exists.

questions.q: What distinguishes the flash-sale checkout latency incident used in Lesson 16 from the other two story beats?
options: It is purely hypothetical and never actually described happening
It already occurred once in an earlier course in the path, and Lesson 16 has students replay it as a drill against their own infrastructure
It has nothing to do with monitoring or the inventory service
It only affects product-catalog, not checkout
questions.explain: The flash-sale incident is canon from the earlier Monitoring, Logging & Observability course. In this capstone's Lesson 16, students re-run it as a tabletop drill, diagnose it with the monitoring stack from Lesson 14, and write a blameless postmortem.

questions.q: What is the RED method, referenced as part of the monitoring requirement in the done checklist?
options: A Terraform state-locking strategy
A dashboard pattern tracking rate, errors, and duration
A Git branching convention for release branches
A naming scheme for Kubernetes namespaces
questions.explain: The RED method — rate, errors, duration — is the dashboard pattern Grafana dashboards use for both services, part of the 'monitored with alerting' item on the definition-of-done checklist.
